ko.executive_summary: SK hynix is ramping nationwide hiring and revamping recruitment to focus on AI-era talent, including eliminating educational requirements and introducing half-day interviews to assess fundamental problem-solving ability. Nvidia plans a Shanghai R&D center to strengthen China presence, while enterprise leaders show broad robotics adoption expectations despite readiness gaps.
key_facts: SK hynix: nationwide briefings with 4,000 applicants, four hub locations (Seoul, Daegu, Cheongju, Gwangju)
SK hynix eliminating education requirements for new recruits
SK hynix implementing half-day interview format for AI talent
Six in ten senior leaders expect robot fleet operations within five years
67% of leaders believe readiness for mixed human-robot workforce by 2030
Nvidia establishing Shanghai R&D Center
74% of leaders predict full-scale robotics could double operational output

implications.text: SK hynix overhaul signals intense competition for AI specialists; educational meritocracy elimination reflects fundamental shift in hiring philosophy toward applied problem-solving capability.
60% of leaders expect robot fleet deployments within five years, but only 40% report readiness; this signals upcoming bottleneck in workforce training and operational integration.
Nvidia Shanghai R&D expansion reflects critical role of China market in HPC ecosystem development despite geopolitical constraints.

ko.counterpoint: High expectations for robotics adoption may not translate to actual capex and integration spending if operational readiness barriers prove more severe than anticipated.

ko.executive_summary: Google is consolidating custom silicon strategy through major partnerships: $12.18 billion warrant deal with Marvell for AI chips with Korea-bound supply shift, and Waymo's custom 5nm 1,000 TOPS robotaxi chip entering mass production. Waymo is actively reducing reliance on Nvidia acceleration, while Anthropic has pre-committed $250 million to Fractile for unshipped silicon.
key_facts: Google-Marvell partnership: up to $12.18 billion in warrants
Marvell equity tied to Korea-bound supply shift
Waymo custom chip: 5nm, 1,000 TOPS, mass production commenced
Waymo chip performance comparable to Nvidia's latest systems
Anthropic pre-revenue contract: $250 million commitment to Fractile
Waymo reducing Nvidia reliance through custom silicon
Wedbush analyzing rumored Google-AMD chip partnership

implications.text: Google's dual strategy (Marvell partnership + Waymo custom chip) signals broader industry move from GPU generalists to task-specific silicon; significant margin pressure on Nvidia in workload-optimized segments.
Marvell warrant structure linking equity to Korea production suggests Google securing geographic redundancy and hedging Taiwan-only concentration risk for AI acceleration.
Anthropic's $250M commitment to Fractile's unshipped silicon indicates confidence in custom silicon viability and willingness to fund unproven startups—normalizing pre-production capital allocation.
Waymo's in-house chip development directly competes with Nvidia's automotive acceleration offerings; mass production signals viable alternative for Level 4+ autonomous platforms.

ko.counterpoint: Google's custom chip investments risk duplicating design and verification complexity; time-to-production delays could erode competitive advantage if Nvidia or AMD accelerators improve workload fit faster.
